description: A normal standup: four categories exercised, three cards created, one item held on a category dispute, one duplicate skipped, and a post-write audit that confirms the board matches the plan.
note:
History up to 2026-08-12 (the system/user prompt split, and why item 5 categorizes as SUBTASK rather than UPDATE) is unchanged from before and is preserved below.

Re-derived again after the category-dispute gate widened from a new-vs-existing-boundary check to a write-equivalence check: it now compares what each read would actually WRITE (create / comment / create-child / nothing / link), not the category label. Item 5 (the flaky-auth-test investigation) is 2a=SUBTASK (create-child) vs 2b=UPDATE (comment) — a different write either way, so it now HOLDS instead of trusting 2a. This is the gate correctly catching a case the old boundary rule was blind to, not a regression.

The caveat the old note raised still applies and is worth restating: whether 2b's blind read agrees with 2a on this specific borderline item is a model judgement that varied across three consecutive re-recordings (held, then not, then not) before this change, and there is no reason to expect it stopped varying now — a future re-record could see 2b agree with 2a (both SUBTASK) and this item go clean again. The dispute RULE is proven deterministically regardless — contractGates.test.ts and an end-to-end hold in run.test.ts, all with scripted replies — this golden only pins what the current recording happens to produce.

— Prior note (2026-08-12) — Pass 1 sometimes extracted a seventh item from the bare status line "Main flow is drafted"; that line was reworded to subordinate it to the actual commitment, the same fix scenario 02 got for the same reason. The evidence that the system/user prompt split itself was behaviourally neutral: Pass 1's prompt fingerprint is byte-identical across the change (ced7582a8aee both sides) while its reply differed, and a paired A/B of the same 2a prompt sent split versus joined returned the same verdict on three consecutive runs.
